name: Predictability-Calibrated Optimistic Adam
parent_evidence: HJ component handoff found D/E/full transfer harmful after a locally positive G state
HNEK full100 changes sign repeatedly through 12000 rather than at one monotone exit point
PHRSUP found the native gradient already reduced the selected local defect while long-horizon quality still reversed
DT/HJ/HNEK update-local repairs therefore do not explain coupled last-iterate oscillation
literature_basis: Daskalakis et al., Training GANs with Optimism, arXiv:1711.00141
Liang and Stokes, Interaction Matters, AISTATS 2019, PMLR 89
unsb_object: native Adam displacement field of the coupled generator, discriminator and entropy-critic game
mathematical_update: For each player p in {G,D,E}, let u_t^p be its native Adam displacement and u_{t-1}^p the previous native displacement. Set rho_t^p=clip(<u_t^p,u_{t-1}^p>/||u_{t-1}^p||^2,0,1) and apply u_*^p=u_t^p+rho_t^p(u_t^p-u_{t-1}^p). F retains native Adam.
derivation: Optimistic mirror descent uses 2u_t-u_{t-1} and has last-iterate convergence in bilinear zero-sum games where ordinary gradient dynamics cycle.
The current clean UNSB game is stochastic and three-player, so unconditional optimism is not justified on every batch.

rho is the clipped least-squares coefficient with which the previous native displacement predicts the current one; it recovers OMD when predictability is one and returns native Adam under anti-alignment or no predictive power.
If the native displacement field is unchanged, u_t-u_{t-1}=0 and the optimistic correction self-nulls exactly even though rho=1.
The first update is native, optimizer moments remain the canonical Adam moments, and only parameter displacement is reflected.
Applying the same rule to G, D and E addresses game interaction; F is not an adversarial player and remains native.
long_horizon_property: reduces to optimistic last-iterate dynamics in a predictable rotational game and self-nulls under stable, nonpredictive or anti-aligned native displacement fields
self_null_condition: the native game field is stable or its previous displacement is not a useful current predictor
unbiased_or_invariance_property: native objectives, endpoint law, Adam moment recurrences and every fixed point are unchanged
paired_target_proof: rho uses only current and previous native optimizer displacements
expected_valid_states: predictable rotational G-D-E dynamics where local mechanism-specific corrections are later counteracted by opponent adaptation
falsification_test: kill if first-step identity, stable-field self-null, full optimizer-state resume or paired blindness fails; permit one revision only if optimism measurably reduces update-field rotation but 400/800 quality remains late-negative
compute_cost: native forward/backward count; one additional parameter snapshot and vector correction per G/D/E update
memory_cost: one previous native displacement plus one transient parameter snapshot per G/D/E parameter
allowed_claim: tests whether long-horizon reversal is primarily a coupled-game last-iterate problem rather than an endpoint defect
forbidden_claims: global convergence for nonconvex three-player UNSB
